# HTML Charts – full reference

> 41 free Chart.js charts for dashboards. Each reads a grid on the same page and redraws it – no API, no install, and no data leaves the browser.

Author: Kai Jones, data analyst – https://kaijxnes.com · Source: https://github.com/kaijxnes/HTML-Charts · Site: https://viz.kaijxnes.com/

## How every chart works

1. Put a grid (or any HTML table) with the chart's column headers on the same page.
2. Add a placeholder: <div data-chart-embed="CHART-ID" style="height:100%"></div>
3. Load the chart script with its SRI hash (copy the loader from the chart's page).
The chart finds the headers (spaces and capitals ignored), reads every row – scrolling grids that only draw what's on screen – and redraws when the grid changes. Nothing is uploaded.

## Placeholder options

- data-columns: map your header names to the chart's keys, e.g. data-columns='{"v1":"Revenue","units":"Customers"}'
- data-labels: shorter on-screen names, same keys
- data-title: replaces the heading
- data-lower-better: metrics where a fall is good, e.g. '["v2"]'
- data-min-volume: Monthly Bars only – flags months with fewer Units
- data-grid-class / data-scroll-class: grid container and scroll box classes for grids that draw rows in batches (MicroStrategy: mstrmojo-Xtab / mstrmojo-scrollNode)

## Platforms

- MicroStrategy: HTML container (HTML Text) with the grid on the same page – works as-is.
- Any web page: table plus snippet – works as-is.
- Tableau: dashboard extension that writes worksheet summary data into a table, then loads the chart.
- Looker: custom visualization that writes query results into a table.
- Power BI: only as a custom visual (pbiviz) with the chart bundled in.
- Qlik Sense: extension that writes the hypercube into a table.

## Charts

### Monthly Bars

A $ metric by month as bars, with a toggle between three metrics, 6-month average cards and a second metric as a line.

When to use it: Use it when you track one value per month and want to see the trend, how recent months compare with the six-month average, and whether thin months can be trusted.
Questions it answers: Is this month above or below our recent average? Which months had too few units to rely on? How does the 18- or 24-month view compare with 12?

Page: https://viz.kaijxnes.com/monthly-bars.html
Script: https://viz.kaijxnes.com/charts/monthly-bars-1.1.0.js
Placeholder id: monthly-bars
Columns:
- Month Key (key month, required): One bar per month (e.g. 202608).
- Metric 1 (key v12, required): $ value per unit. Metric 2 and Metric 3 add the toggle.
- Metric 1 Avg (key a12, optional): Filled for the latest 6 months only – drives the average cards (also Metric 2/3 Avg).
- Units (key units, optional): Units – how many users, customers or orders – drawn as the line.
- Month Index (key idx, optional): Used to order months if the month key can't be read.
Features:
- Bars for the chosen metric by month; click a card or button to switch
- Cards with the 6-month average of each metric
- Dashed average line; months outside the window are faded
- Units as a line on its own axis
- Optional low-volume flag: add data-min-volume="600" to stripe and badge months with fewer Units than that (on in this demo)

### Stacked Segments

Metric × units by month, stacked by segment (any combination of three dimensions), with filters and a ranking.

When to use it: Use it when a monthly total is made up of segments and you need to see which combinations drive it – for example channel × product.
Questions it answers: Which segment combination contributes most each month? How does a filtered selection compare with the rest? Is value per unit rising or falling?

Page: https://viz.kaijxnes.com/stacked-segments.html
Script: https://viz.kaijxnes.com/charts/stacked-segments-1.1.0.js
Placeholder id: stacked-segments
Columns:
- Month Key (key month, required): One bar per month.
- Units (key units, required): Units – how many users, customers or orders in the row – total = Metric × Units.
- Metric 1 (key v12, required): $ value per unit. Metric 2/3 add the toggle.
- Dimension A (key dimA, optional): Segment and filter.
- Dimension B (key dimB, optional): Segment and filter.
- Dimension C (key dimC, optional): Segment and filter.
- Month Index (key idx, optional): Optional.
Features:
- Segments from any combination of Dimension A, B and C (e.g. A1 × B2)
- Multi-select filters; the selection is compared with the total
- Ranking of every segment with share, count and value per unit
- Value-per-unit line over the stacked bars
- Reads grids of thousands of rows by scrolling through them (for grids that draw rows in batches)
- Loading screen until every row is read; Read details log for troubleshooting

### Segment Breakdown

The stacked segment view for grids with the month first and two dimensions – starts on Dimension A, combine with Dimension C.

When to use it: Use it when your grid starts with the month and has one or two dimensions, and you want a stacked view you can split and filter.
Questions it answers: Which segment contributes most each month? How do two dimensions combine? What share of the total does the top segment hold?

Page: https://viz.kaijxnes.com/segment-breakdown.html
Script: https://viz.kaijxnes.com/charts/segment-breakdown-1.1.0.js
Placeholder id: segment-breakdown
Columns:
- Month Key (key month, required): One bar per month (can be the first column).
- Units (key units, required): Units – how many users, customers or orders in the row.
- Metric 1 (key v12, required): $ value per unit.
- Dimension A (key dimA, optional): Segment and filter.
- Dimension C (key dimC, optional): Segment and filter.
- Month Index (key idx, optional): Optional.
Features:
- Starts on Dimension A; click Dimension C to combine them
- Metric toggle hides itself when the grid only has Metric 1
- Merged labels are carried down to every row
- Handles grids with a frozen header and batch-loaded rows
- Same filters, ranking and loading screen as Stacked Segments

### Cost vs Return

Cost against return (units × value) by month: net return, ROI, cost per unit vs value per unit and a monthly table.

When to use it: Use it when you spend money each month to get units, and want to know whether what they're worth covers what they cost.
Questions it answers: What's our ROI and ROAS this period? Is cost per unit below value per unit? Which months lost money?

Page: https://viz.kaijxnes.com/cost-vs-return.html
Script: https://viz.kaijxnes.com/charts/cost-vs-return-1.1.0.js
Placeholder id: cost-vs-return
Columns:
- Month Key (key month, required): Month. Rows without one are left out.
- Cost (key cost, required): $ cost for the month.
- Units (key units, required): Units – how many users, customers or orders – used for cost per unit and return.
- Metric 1 (key v12, required): $ value per unit; return = Units × Metric 1.
- Month Index (key idx, optional): Optional.
Features:
- Net return, ROI and ROAS, cost, return, cost per unit and count cards
- Cost vs return bars with an ROI line and break-even marker
- Cost per unit vs value per unit, shaded green where value is higher
- Monthly table with totals
- Rows with no month key are left out and counted in the subtitle

### Month Heatmap

A heatmap of a $ metric by start month and month index – per month, cumulative or per unit – with every month's curve against the average.

When to use it: Use it for cohort-style data: groups that start in a month and build up value over the months after – the classic triangle view.
Questions it answers: Which start months perform best after six months? How quickly does value build up after the start? Are newer groups ahead of or behind older ones?

Page: https://viz.kaijxnes.com/month-heatmap.html
Script: https://viz.kaijxnes.com/charts/month-heatmap-1.1.0.js
Placeholder id: month-heatmap
Columns:
- Month Key (key month, required): The start month – one heatmap row each.
- Month Index (key idx, required): Months since the start month (0, 1, 2 …) – one column each.
- Metric 1 (key v1, required): $ value for that month and index.
- Units (key units, optional): Units – how many users, customers or orders – index 0 is the base for the per-unit view.
Features:
- Heatmap shaded within each index column, so later columns stay readable
- Per month, cumulative and per-unit views (per unit = cumulative ÷ the month's Units at index 0)
- Average row, plus a line chart of every month's curve against the average
- Cards for the total, the average at the furthest index most months have reached, and the best month
- Months are sorted by their key; merged month labels are carried down

### KPI Scorecard

Up to six metrics as cards with the latest value, change vs the previous month, a 3-month average or last year, and a sparkline; click one for its trend.

When to use it: Use it as the top strip of a dashboard: the latest value of each key metric, its change and a sparkline, with one click to the full trend.
Questions it answers: How did each KPI move against last month or last year? Which metrics are trending the wrong way? What did the scorecard look like in a past month?

Page: https://viz.kaijxnes.com/kpi-scorecard.html
Script: https://viz.kaijxnes.com/charts/kpi-scorecard-1.1.0.js
Placeholder id: kpi-scorecard
Columns:
- Month Key (key month, required): One point per month; several rows in a month are added together.
- Metric 1 (key v1, required): Any metric – $, % or a count is read from the grid's own formatting.
- Metric 2 … Metric 6 (key v2 … v6, optional): Up to five more metrics; cards only appear for the ones in the grid.
Features:
- Cards with the latest value, the change and a 12-month sparkline
- Compare to the previous month, the 3-month average or the same month last year
- Pick any month with “As of” to see the scorecard at that point
- Percentages are averaged and compared in points; $ and counts are totalled and compared in %
- Mark metrics where lower is better with data-lower-better='["v3"]' so a fall shows green (Metric 3 in this demo)
- Click a card for a 24-month bar chart with a 3-month rolling average

### Time Series Trio

Three metrics, each on its own row: a scorecard for the latest 7/28/90 days or months against the period before, next to a chart of all the data over time.

When to use it: Use it when a few metrics each deserve their own row: a scorecard for the latest 7, 28 or 90 days next to the full history.
Questions it answers: How did the last 28 days compare with the 28 before? What's the daily average and peak day? Is the trend weekly-seasonal or steady?

Page: https://viz.kaijxnes.com/time-series-trio.html
Script: https://viz.kaijxnes.com/charts/time-series-trio-1.1.0.js
Placeholder id: time-series-trio
Columns:
- Date (key date, required): A daily date (2026-10-23, 23/10/2026, 23 Oct 2026) or a month key (202610). Several rows on a date are added together.
- Metric 1 (key v1, required): Any metric – $, % or a count, read from the grid's formatting.
- Metric 2 (key v2, optional): Second row.
- Metric 3 (key v3, optional): Third row.
Features:
- Scorecard per metric: latest range total, change vs the same-length range before, average and peak
- Range buttons: 7, 28, 90 days or 12 months for daily data; 1, 3, 6 or 12 months for monthly data
- Chart grouping: daily, weekly or monthly (monthly or quarterly for monthly data)
- The latest range is shaded on each chart, the range it's compared with faintly
- Percentages are averaged and compared in points; $ and counts are totalled
- Mark metrics where lower is better with data-lower-better='["v2"]'

### Funnel

Counts through ordered stages as a funnel, with step and overall conversion, the biggest drop-off and a conversion curve per segment.

When to use it: Use it for any process with ordered steps – sign-up to purchase, lead to deal – to see where people drop out.
Questions it answers: Where is the biggest drop-off? What's the overall conversion from first to last step? Which segment converts best at each step?

Page: https://viz.kaijxnes.com/funnel.html
Script: https://viz.kaijxnes.com/charts/funnel-1.1.0.js
Placeholder id: funnel
Columns:
- Stage (key stage, required): Stage name – stages keep the order they first appear in the grid.
- Metric 1 (key v1, required): Count at that stage.
- Dimension A (key dimA, optional): Optional segment – adds buttons and a curve per segment.
Features:
- Funnel bars sized against the first stage
- % of previous stage and % of first stage on every step, with the drop between steps
- Cards for overall conversion, top and end of funnel and the biggest drop-off
- Segment buttons (top 6 by size) and a line per segment showing % of the first stage reaching each stage

### Change Bridge

A waterfall from one total to another, showing how much each item added or took away – e.g. last period to this period.

When to use it: Use it to explain why a total moved between two periods, by showing what each item added or took away.
Questions it answers: What drove the change from last period to this one? Which items grew and which shrank? How much did the smaller items add up to?

Page: https://viz.kaijxnes.com/change-bridge.html
Script: https://viz.kaijxnes.com/charts/change-bridge-1.1.0.js
Placeholder id: change-bridge
Columns:
- Dimension A (key dimA, required): The item each step belongs to.
- Metric 1 (key v1, required): The before value (e.g. last period).
- Metric 2 (key v2, required): The after value (e.g. this period).
Features:
- Bridge from the before total to the after total, one step per item
- Order by biggest change or keep the grid's order; small items grouped into Other
- Rises in green, falls in red, labels on every step
- Cards for the change, start, end, biggest rise and biggest fall
- Ranked list of every item's change with before → after

### Pareto

Items ranked largest first with a cumulative share line, showing how few items make up 80% of the total.

When to use it: Use it to find the vital few: how many items make up most of a total, and which ones they are.
Questions it answers: How many items make up 80% of the total? How dependent are we on the top item? Where does the long tail start?

Page: https://viz.kaijxnes.com/pareto.html
Script: https://viz.kaijxnes.com/charts/pareto-1.1.0.js
Placeholder id: pareto
Columns:
- Dimension A (key dimA, required): The item – rows with the same item are added together.
- Metric 1 (key v1, required): The value to rank by.
Features:
- Bars largest first, coloured by whether they fall inside the first 80%
- Cumulative share line with an 80% marker
- Top 10 / 20 / 50 / All
- Cards for how many items make 80%, the total, the top item and the top-5 share

### Target Pacing

Month-to-date actual against target by day, with a month-end projection, % of target and the daily rate needed to hit it.

When to use it: Use it during a month to see whether you're on track to hit target, and what each remaining day needs to deliver.
Questions it answers: Are we ahead or behind target so far this month? Where will we land at month end? How much do we need per day to hit target?

Page: https://viz.kaijxnes.com/target-pacing.html
Script: https://viz.kaijxnes.com/charts/target-pacing-1.1.0.js
Placeholder id: target-pacing
Columns:
- Date (key date, required): A daily date. Future days can have a target and no actual.
- Metric 1 (key v1, required): The actual for the day.
- Metric 2 (key v2, optional): The target for the day – without it you get a run-rate projection.
Features:
- Daily bars with cumulative actual and cumulative target lines
- Month-end projection on the target's daily shape (or the run rate if there's no target)
- Cards for actual and target to date, projected month end and the daily rate needed
- Pick any month in the grid

### Quadrant Scatter

Each item plotted by two metrics, sized by a third, split into four quadrants at the averages – spot the high-value, low-cost winners.

When to use it: Use it to compare items on two measures at once and sort them into four groups – high/high winners, and the ones to fix.
Questions it answers: Which items are high on both measures? Which are high cost but low value? Are the biggest items in the right quadrant?

Page: https://viz.kaijxnes.com/quadrant-scatter.html
Script: https://viz.kaijxnes.com/charts/quadrant-scatter-1.1.0.js
Placeholder id: quadrant-scatter
Columns:
- Dimension A (key dimA, required): The item – one bubble each; several rows are combined.
- Metric 1 (key v1, required): Across (x).
- Metric 2 (key v2, required): Up (y).
- Metric 3 (key v3, optional): Bubble size.
Features:
- Bubbles coloured by quadrant, with dashed average lines
- Cards counting the items in each quadrant, with examples
- Labels for the top 8, all or none
- Percentages are averaged per item; $ and counts are totalled

### Mix Shift

How the share of a total moves between segments month by month, as 100% stacked bars with gains and losses in points.

When to use it: Use it when the total matters less than how it's split, and you want to see which segments are gaining or losing share.
Questions it answers: Which segment gained the most share this year? Is the mix shifting even if the total is flat? What share does the largest segment hold now?

Page: https://viz.kaijxnes.com/mix-shift.html
Script: https://viz.kaijxnes.com/charts/mix-shift-1.1.0.js
Placeholder id: mix-shift
Columns:
- Month Key (key month, required): One bar per month.
- Dimension A (key dimA, required): The segment – the top 6 shown, the rest grouped as Other.
- Metric 1 (key v1, required): The value to split.
Features:
- Share % or values view
- Cards for the largest segment and the biggest gain and loss in share since the first month
- List of every segment's share first month → latest, in points

### Calendar Heatmap

A daily metric laid out as a calendar, one square per day, with averages by weekday and totals by month.

When to use it: Use it for daily data to spot patterns by weekday, season and streak at a glance.
Questions it answers: Which weekday is strongest? Are there seasonal highs and lows? When were the best and worst days?

Page: https://viz.kaijxnes.com/calendar-heatmap.html
Script: https://viz.kaijxnes.com/charts/calendar-heatmap-1.1.0.js
Placeholder id: calendar-heatmap
Columns:
- Date (key date, required): A daily date.
- Metric 1 (key v1, required): The value for the day.
Features:
- Calendar of the last 12 months or any year, shaded in five levels
- Cards for the total, best day, strongest weekday, best month and longest run above the median
- Average by weekday and totals by month

### Year over Year

A metric by calendar month for this year against the two before, monthly or year to date, with the YTD change.

When to use it: Use it for any monthly metric with seasonality, to compare this year with the last two month by month and year to date.
Questions it answers: Are we ahead of last year so far? How many months beat the same month last year? Does this year follow the usual seasonal shape?

Page: https://viz.kaijxnes.com/year-over-year.html
Script: https://viz.kaijxnes.com/charts/year-over-year-1.1.0.js
Placeholder id: year-over-year
Columns:
- Month Key (key month, required): Month (e.g. 202609) – daily dates are rolled up to months.
- Metric 1 (key v1, required): The value.
Features:
- This year against the previous two, Jan–Dec
- Monthly or cumulative year-to-date lines
- Cards for YTD vs the same months last year, the latest month vs last year, months ahead and the best month
- Pick any year in the grid

### Leaderboard

A ranked table for any month with change vs the month before, rank movement, share, a 12-month total and a trend sparkline.

When to use it: Use it to rank entries – teams, products, regions – for any month, with how they moved and a 12-month trend for each.
Questions it answers: Who's number one this month and for how long? Who climbed or fell the most places? Which entries are trending up?

Page: https://viz.kaijxnes.com/leaderboard.html
Script: https://viz.kaijxnes.com/charts/leaderboard-1.1.0.js
Placeholder id: leaderboard
Columns:
- Month Key (key month, required): Month.
- Dimension A (key dimA, required): The entry being ranked.
- Metric 1 (key v1, required): The value to rank by.
Features:
- Rank by the month's value, the change or the last 12 months
- Rank movement arrows against the month before
- Cards for number 1, the total, the biggest climber and the biggest faller
- Pick any month; trend sparklines cover the 12 months to it

### Distribution

A histogram of one value per row (e.g. per customer or order), with median, mean, P10–P90 and how much the top 10% hold – optionally split into groups.

When to use it: Use it when you have one value per row – per customer, order or day – and averages hide what's really going on.
Questions it answers: What's typical: the median or the mean? How wide is the spread? How much of the total comes from the top 10%?

Page: https://viz.kaijxnes.com/distribution.html
Script: https://viz.kaijxnes.com/charts/distribution-1.1.0.js
Placeholder id: distribution
Columns:
- Metric 1 (key v1, required): One value per grid row.
- Dimension A (key dimA, optional): Optional group – up to 4 groups overlaid as % of each group.
Features:
- Automatic bin sizes (or 10 / 20 / 40), with the option to trim the top 1%
- Median and mean marked on the chart
- Cards for median, mean, P10–P90, standard deviation and the top-10% share of the total

### Target Attainment

Actual against target for every item as bullet bars, coloured by % of target, with the overall position and who's furthest ahead or behind.

When to use it: Use it to show every item's actual against its own target, so it's obvious who's ahead and who needs help.
Questions it answers: How many items are on target? Who's furthest behind and by how much? What's the overall attainment?

Page: https://viz.kaijxnes.com/target-attainment.html
Script: https://viz.kaijxnes.com/charts/target-attainment-1.1.0.js
Placeholder id: target-attainment
Columns:
- Dimension A (key dimA, required): The item.
- Metric 1 (key v1, required): Actual.
- Metric 2 (key v2, required): Target.
Features:
- A bar per item with a target marker; green at 100%+, amber 90–100%, red under 90%
- Sort by % of target, gap, target size or grid order
- Cards for overall %, how many are on target, and the furthest ahead and behind
- For costs, add data-lower-better='["v1"]' so being under target counts as good

### Anomaly Watch

A daily or monthly metric against its rolling average with a normal band, flagging the points that are unusually high or low.

When to use it: Use it to monitor a daily or monthly metric and catch the days that are unusually high or low against recent history.
Questions it answers: Is today's number normal? When did something unusual last happen? How many unusual days were there recently?

Page: https://viz.kaijxnes.com/anomaly-watch.html
Script: https://viz.kaijxnes.com/charts/anomaly-watch-1.1.0.js
Placeholder id: anomaly-watch
Columns:
- Date (key date, required): A daily date or a month key.
- Metric 1 (key v1, required): The value.
Features:
- Expected value = the average of the previous 7 / 14 / 28 days (or 3 / 6 / 12 months)
- Normal band of ±2, 2.5 or 3 standard deviations; points outside it are flagged
- Cards for the latest value vs expected, its status, recent unusual points and the most recent one
- List of every unusual point with how far out it was

### Treemap

Rectangles sized by value, grouped by one dimension and split by a second – click a group to zoom in.

When to use it: Use it to show how a total splits across a hierarchy – groups and the items inside them – in one view.
Questions it answers: Which groups make up most of the total? What's the biggest item inside each group? How concentrated is the total?

Page: https://viz.kaijxnes.com/treemap.html
Script: https://viz.kaijxnes.com/charts/treemap-1.1.0.js
Placeholder id: treemap
Columns:
- Dimension A (key dimA, required): The group.
- Dimension B (key dimB, optional): The items inside each group.
- Metric 1 (key v1, required): The value (positive values only).
Features:
- Squarified layout so tiles stay readable
- Nested view or groups only; click a group to zoom into it
- Cards for the total, the largest item, the top-3 share and the number of items

### Small Multiples

A small chart per segment, side by side, with the latest value and change – on the same scale or each on its own.

When to use it: Use it to compare the trend of many segments side by side without one chart turning into spaghetti.
Questions it answers: Which segments are growing and which are shrinking? Do they share the same seasonal shape? Which segment changed most last month?

Page: https://viz.kaijxnes.com/small-multiples.html
Script: https://viz.kaijxnes.com/charts/small-multiples-1.1.0.js
Placeholder id: small-multiples
Columns:
- Month Key (key month, required): Month (daily dates are rolled up).
- Dimension A (key dimA, required): One tile each – up to 16.
- Metric 1 (key v1, required): The value.
Features:
- One mini chart per segment, coloured by its latest change
- Same scale for fair comparison or own scale to see each shape
- Order by size, growth or name

### Variance Table

A table of up to three metrics by segment for any month against the previous month or last year, with colour-coded changes and totals.

When to use it: Use it when people want the numbers: each segment this month against last month or last year, with the changes coloured.
Questions it answers: Which segments moved most against last month? Is the total up or down on last year? Which metric is driving the change?

Page: https://viz.kaijxnes.com/variance-table.html
Script: https://viz.kaijxnes.com/charts/variance-table-1.1.0.js
Placeholder id: variance-table
Columns:
- Month Key (key month, required): Month.
- Dimension A (key dimA, required): One table row each.
- Metric 1 (key v1, required): First metric.
- Metric 2 (key v2, optional): Second metric.
- Metric 3 (key v3, optional): Third metric.
Features:
- Current, comparison and change columns for each metric, with a total row
- Compare to the previous month or the same month last year; pick any month
- Changes shaded green or red by size; click a column to sort by it
- A card per metric with its total and change

### Gauges

Up to 12 KPIs as dials against their targets, with red/amber/green zones and a target marker.

When to use it: Use it for a handful of headline KPIs with targets, where a dial reads faster than a table.
Questions it answers: Which KPIs are on target? Which one needs attention first? How far off target is each one?

Page: https://viz.kaijxnes.com/gauges.html
Script: https://viz.kaijxnes.com/charts/gauges-1.1.0.js
Placeholder id: gauges
Columns:
- Dimension A (key dimA, required): The KPI name – one dial each.
- Metric 1 (key v1, required): Actual. Each KPI keeps its own $, % or count format.
- Metric 2 (key v2, required): Target.
Features:
- A dial per KPI with zones for under 90%, 90–100% and on target
- Each row can be a different kind of number – $, % or count
- Cards for how many are on target, the best and the one needing attention
- Mark KPIs where lower is better by name: data-lower-better='["Goal 4"]' (on in this demo)

### Combo Chart

Bars for one metric with one or two more as lines on a second axis, grouped by day, week, month, quarter or year.

When to use it: Use it when a volume and a rate belong together – revenue and margin, orders and conversion – on one time axis.
Questions it answers: How do volume and rate move together? Did the rate drop when volume grew? What happened last period vs the one before?

Page: https://viz.kaijxnes.com/combo-chart.html
Script: https://viz.kaijxnes.com/charts/combo-chart-1.1.0.js
Placeholder id: combo-chart
Columns:
- Date (key date, required): A daily date or a month key.
- Metric 1 (key v1, required): Bars.
- Metric 2 (key v2, optional): Line on the right axis.
- Metric 3 (key v3, optional): Second line – shares the right axis if it's the same kind of number.
Features:
- Group daily data by day, week or month, and monthly data by month, quarter or year
- Last 12, last 24 or all periods
- A card per metric with the latest period and its change

### Flow (Sankey)

How a total flows from one dimension to another – e.g. source to outcome – as bands sized by value. Click a node to highlight its flows.

When to use it: Use it to show how a total flows from one category to another – source to outcome, channel to product.
Questions it answers: Where does each source end up? What's the biggest single flow? Which outcome depends most on one source?

Page: https://viz.kaijxnes.com/flow-sankey.html
Script: https://viz.kaijxnes.com/charts/flow-sankey-1.1.0.js
Placeholder id: flow-sankey
Columns:
- Dimension A (key dimA, required): Where it comes from (left).
- Dimension B (key dimB, required): Where it goes (right).
- Metric 1 (key v1, required): The amount flowing (positive values).
Features:
- Up to 9 nodes a side, the rest grouped as Other
- Colour by either side; click a node to highlight just its flows
- Cards for the total, the biggest flow and the largest node on each side

### Box Plot

The spread of a value within each group – median, middle 50%, whiskers, mean and outliers – to compare groups fairly.

When to use it: Use it to compare spreads between groups, not just their averages – who's consistent and who's all over the place.
Questions it answers: Which group has the highest typical value? Which group varies the most? Where are the outliers?

Page: https://viz.kaijxnes.com/box-plot.html
Script: https://viz.kaijxnes.com/charts/box-plot-1.1.0.js
Placeholder id: box-plot
Columns:
- Dimension A (key dimA, required): The group – needs at least 3 values each.
- Metric 1 (key v1, required): One value per grid row.
Features:
- Box for the middle 50%, line for the median, red dot for the mean
- Whiskers to 1.5× the box height, outliers as dots
- Sort by median, spread or name
- Cards for the overall median, the highest and lowest median and the widest spread

### Radar Compare

Compare up to five segments across several metrics on one radar, each metric scored 0–100 against the best segment.

When to use it: Use it to compare the profile of a few segments across several metrics with different units.
Questions it answers: Which segment is strongest overall? Where is each segment weak? Which segment leads on each metric?

Page: https://viz.kaijxnes.com/radar-compare.html
Script: https://viz.kaijxnes.com/charts/radar-compare-1.1.0.js
Placeholder id: radar-compare
Columns:
- Dimension A (key dimA, required): The segment.
- Metric 1 … Metric 6 (key v1 … v6, required): At least 3 metrics – $, % or counts.
Features:
- Scores each metric 0–100 against the best segment, so different units sit on one chart
- Pick up to 5 segments to compare
- Table of the real values with the best on each metric highlighted
- Lower-is-better metrics are scored the other way round (Metric 4 in this demo)

### Bump Chart

How each segment's rank changes month by month – who's rising, who's falling and how often the leader changes.

When to use it: Use it when rank matters more than value: who's first, who's climbing and how often the lead changes.
Questions it answers: Who's held the top spot longest? Who climbed the most places this year? How often did the leader change?

Page: https://viz.kaijxnes.com/bump-chart.html
Script: https://viz.kaijxnes.com/charts/bump-chart-1.1.0.js
Placeholder id: bump-chart
Columns:
- Month Key (key month, required): Month.
- Dimension A (key dimA, required): The entry being ranked.
- Metric 1 (key v1, required): The value to rank by.
Features:
- A line per segment showing its rank each month, labelled at the end
- Top 5 / 8 / 12 / all; click a line to highlight it
- Cards for the leader and its streak, the biggest climb and drop, and how often the lead changed

### Indexed Growth

Every segment's trend indexed to 100 at a base month, so growth can be compared regardless of size.

When to use it: Use it to compare growth between segments of very different sizes by starting them all at 100.
Questions it answers: Which segment grew fastest since a chosen month? Who's growing faster than the total? Which segments are shrinking?

Page: https://viz.kaijxnes.com/indexed-growth.html
Script: https://viz.kaijxnes.com/charts/indexed-growth-1.1.0.js
Placeholder id: indexed-growth
Columns:
- Month Key (key month, required): Month.
- Dimension A (key dimA, required): The segment – the 8 largest are shown.
- Metric 1 (key v1, required): The value.
Features:
- Lines for each segment and the total, all starting at 100
- Pick any base month
- Cards for total growth, the fastest and slowest, and how many beat the total

### Dumbbell

Before and after for every item as two joined dots, coloured by whether it got better or worse.

When to use it: Use it for before-and-after comparisons across many items – last year vs this year, before vs after a change.
Questions it answers: How many items improved? Which improved or fell the most? Did the overall figure go up?

Page: https://viz.kaijxnes.com/dumbbell.html
Script: https://viz.kaijxnes.com/charts/dumbbell-1.1.0.js
Placeholder id: dumbbell
Columns:
- Dimension A (key dimA, required): The item.
- Metric 1 (key v1, required): Before.
- Metric 2 (key v2, required): After.
Features:
- A dot for before and after on one shared scale, joined by a line
- Sort by change, by the after value or keep grid order
- Cards for how many improved, the biggest rise and fall and the overall change
- Percentages compare in points; mark lower-is-better with data-lower-better

### Correlation Matrix

How strongly up to six metrics move together across rows, as a colour-coded matrix – click a cell to see the scatter.

When to use it: Use it to explore which metrics move together across rows before building a model or a story.
Questions it answers: Which metrics rise and fall together? Is there a negative relationship worth checking? What does the scatter of any pair look like?

Page: https://viz.kaijxnes.com/correlation-matrix.html
Script: https://viz.kaijxnes.com/charts/correlation-matrix-1.1.0.js
Placeholder id: correlation-matrix
Columns:
- Metric 1 … Metric 6 (key v1 … v6, required): At least 2 metrics; each grid row is one observation.
- Dimension A (key dimA, optional): Optional label shown on the scatter tooltip.
Features:
- Pearson correlation for every pair, green for positive and red for negative
- Click a cell for a scatter of that pair with a trend line
- Cards for the strongest positive and negative links

### Time Series Stack

Up to six metrics, each on its own row with a latest-range scorecard and a chart of all the data over time.

When to use it: Use it when you want the Time Series Trio layout for more metrics – up to six rows, each with a scorecard and full history.
Questions it answers: How did each of six metrics move over the latest range? Which metrics are up and which are down? Where are the peaks across all of them?

Placeholder id: time-series-stack
Columns:

- Metric 1 … Metric 6 (key v1 … v6, required): 1 to 6 metrics – a row appears for each one in the grid.
Features:
- Everything the Time Series Trio does, for up to six metrics
- Range buttons: 7, 28, 90 days or 12 months (1, 3, 6, 12 months for monthly data)
- Daily, weekly or monthly chart grouping, with the latest range shaded
